Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: "Alright, hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna keep this tight — year end short brief, some context, and then the thermostat — what we change. Uh, quick housekeeping: recording is on, slide deck in the chat. Okay Maya, kick us off with the product pulse."

[00:28] Maya Singh: "Cool, thanks Jordan. Uh — hi team. Quick product hill: Q4 shipped the continuous batching improvements, the KV cache bugfix, and the first pass of quantization profiles. Those are in prod for hosted, and we've got canary traffic on Dedicated in EU-west-1. We're seeing token cost reductions in the pilot by about 12% but, um, latency variance in tail p95 is still up a bit when bursts happen. We're tracking telemetry and have a remediation path but it requires a little infra spend and one extra eng sprint."

[01:12] Sara Li: "To add — the tail p95 is tied to our current batching window heuristics; we can tighten the latency SLOs but we lose a percentage of the batching savings. So, tradeoff is pretty direct: latency vs unit cost. We'll put sample numbers in the memo."

[01:45] Jordan Kim: "Thanks. Priya, burn/runway quick stat?"

[01:52] Priya Desai: "Short version: runway is about 14 months at current burn, but that assumes no material sales acceleration. If we maintain hiring as planned we drop to ~10–11 months. I have a month-by-month in the board packet — I'll send a trimmed version after this. We need to decide on the hiring posture today because that materially affects the ask."

[02:20] Jordan Kim: "Right. So high-level decision: immediate hold on non-essential hiring; exceptions allowed for customer-critical roles and revenue engines. Alex — you have the proposed exception flow?"

[02:32] Alex Rivera: "Yes. We propose a two-tier exceptions process: Tier 1 — revenue/sales-critical, auto-approve with AE/Finance sign-off; Tier 2 — product/infra, needs leadership review weekly. We also require a 90-day review on any hire approved during freeze. I'll circulate the exact template and the sample list."

[03:00] Ben Ortiz (Sales): "One ask from Customer Success: three PoC customers in pipeline need Dedicated proof-of-concept resources. If we don't staff those, we risk losing momentum and renewal. We'll put numbers in — but they're high-leverage. If Dedicated capacity is the constraint, can we shift some hosted burst capacity instead?"

[03:35] Ethan Lowe: "We can, but we must be careful on tenancy and data isolation. For a prioritized set we can offer hosted burst under NDA, or we can fast-track private packages but that increases ops burden. We'll prepare a short cost/time matrix. Also worth noting: Private deployments require an updated packaging artifact; our on-prem bundle has a known installer edge-case for older kube versions — it's the thing that reads as 'kube-proxy oddness' in some logs. We mislabelled it in the ticket as KV cash earlier — apologies for the transcript."

[04:12] Jordan Kim: "Security/compliance quick check — where are we on SOC2 and ISO?"

[04:18] Maya Singh: "SOC2 Type II audit is on track; we have one open control around key rotation docs with KMS. We also have a runbook gap for emergency key rotation — that's on Ethan + Security's list. ISO intake requires a little more documentation for our VPC/private installers; we'll include that in the packaging memo."

[04:45] Camille Park (Ops): "On Private packaging — ops has a small backlog to harden the installer and provide clearer networking docs — e.g., examples for VPC peering and the NATting rules that folks trip on. We'll publish a 'first run' checklist for customers."

[05:10] Jordan Kim: "Competitive posture — any signals?"

[05:15] Ben Ortiz: "We saw two competitors publish price cuts and new managed private tiers, so we should be prepared for procurement conversations. Also, a couple of customers asked about OpenModelHub integrations — specifically faster on-disk quant files. That's probably in product backlog but a lower priority."

[05:44] Jordan Kim: "OK. So let's align: hiring pause, exceptions for revenue-critical, commit to the memos on Dedicated vs Private and the cost tradeoffs, and produce the budget ask. Maya, you will own the roadmap snapshot; Ethan + Sara will own the infra memo; Priya will own the burn table; Alex to publish the headcount exceptions process. Any pushback?"

[06:12] Sara Li: "One thing — if we freeze hiring we should not freeze essential reliability work. The risk is accumulating tech debt that will amplify costs in H2. We want explicit carve-outs for reliability engineering."

[06:30] Jordan Kim: "Agreed. We'll set reliability as an exception bucket with approval. Alex, include that."

[06:40] Jordan Kim (audience question): "There's a question in the Q&A about Dedicated SLOs and what we promise to customers — short answer?"

[06:48] Ethan Lowe: "Dedicated SLA is currently drafted at 99.9% with a latency SLO per model family. We need to finalize the p95/p99 numbers by Jan 10 and have the canary benchmarks across our top five model families. We'll run two public benchmarks and one closed enterprise test. I'll coordinate with SEs."

[07:20] Audience (unmuted): "Is there any plan to open-source any of the kernel optimizations?"

[07:27] Maya Singh: "Short answer: some low-risk bits like telemetry helpers we plan to open-source; core runtime kernel changes are sensitive and probably not this quarter. We'll publish a list of candidate components."

[07:45] Jordan Kim: "Alright, quick recap for the record and next steps."

[07:50] Jordan Kim: "1) Hiring freeze effective immediately, exceptions process to be circulated; 2) Priya will produce runway tables for board; 3) Maya publishes Q1 snapshot; 4) Ethan + Sara produce Dedicated vs Private cost/ops memo with bench numbers; 5) People publishes exception flow and reliability carve-outs; 6) Ops publishes the Private 'first-run' checklist. Expect these items to land in the company channel and via email."

[08:28] Alex Rivera: "I'll also schedule a follow-on leadership sync to review exception requests every Friday this month. I'll send the calendar invite."

[08:35] Jordan Kim: "Great. Last thing — thanks team for the fast work this year. I know it's been intense. We will frame the budget ask for the board and make targeted asks rather than a big broad spend. Closeout: if you have sensitive items please flag them to me and Priya offline. Meeting adjourned."

[09:00] End of recording.
